title: Removal of Tractor Powertrain System Components and Parts

lessons.title: Preparing to remove powertrain parts
lessons.html:
What is the powertrain?

The powertrain carries power from the engine to the wheels. It includes the clutch, gearbox, PTO, differential, final drives, front axle drive shaft and front axle. These parts are big and heavy. Removing them is team work, led by the mechanic.

Your tasks

  • Help prepare the tractor and work area.
  • Drain oils and label parts.
  • Help support and move heavy sections safely.
  • Keep parts, bolts and shims in order.

Preparing the tractor

  1. Wash the tractor if it is very dirty, especially around joints.
  2. Park on a level, hard floor with enough room around it.
  3. Lower implements and remove them if the mechanic says so.
  4. Chock the wheels and take the key out.
  5. Disconnect the battery negative lead.

Draining oil

Gearbox and axle oil can be a lot of litres. Use a big enough drip tray or drum. Open the drain plugs and let the oil run out. Look at the oil and the drain plug magnet. Tell the mechanic if you see metal pieces, a milky colour or a burnt smell. Keep a sample if asked.

Disconnecting

  • Take photos of all linkages, hoses and wiring.
  • Label every wire and hose.
  • Cap all hydraulic lines and openings.
  • Remove the drive shaft guard and the front drive shaft, supporting it so it does not fall.

Equipment for heavy parts

The mechanic will use splitting stands or trolleys, axle stands, a crane or hoist, and wooden wedges. Check that all equipment is rated for the weight and is in good condition. Tell the mechanic if anything looks damaged.

lessons.title: Splitting the tractor and removing parts
lessons.html:
Splitting the tractor

On most tractors there is no separate chassis. The engine, gearbox and rear axle bolt together to make the frame. To reach the clutch or gearbox, the tractor must be split into two parts.

Safety first

  • Both halves must be held up by proper splitting stands or stands under the right points.
  • Wedge the front axle so the front section cannot tip sideways.
  • Never hold a tractor section on a jack or loader only.
  • Keep hands and feet away when sections move. They can crush you.
  • Only the mechanic gives the signals. Everyone else listens and waits.

Steps the team follows

  1. Support the front and rear halves.
  2. Remove the joining bolts a few at a time as the mechanic directs.
  3. Roll the halves apart slowly and keep them straight.
  4. Lock the stands or trolleys so they cannot move.

Removing the clutch

The mechanic marks the pressure plate and flywheel. Bolts are loosened a little at a time, in a crisscross pattern, so the plate does not bend. Hold the clutch so it does not fall. The disc goes on a clean bench. Do not touch the friction face with oily hands.

Removing other powertrain parts

  • Final drives and hubs: heavy; use a crane or jack with an adaptor.
  • PTO parts: keep shafts, gears and bearings in order.
  • Front axle: support with a cradle or stands before removing pivot pins.

Keeping order

Lay parts out in order. Keep shims and washers with their parts in labelled bags; the mechanic needs them to set up gears later. Cover open housings with clean plastic so dirt and dust do not fall in.

Recording

Write on the job card what was removed, oil drained and anything unusual. Dispose of oil in the used oil drum.

Key points

  • The powertrain includes clutch, gearbox, PTO, differential, final drives and front axle.
  • Check drained oil for metal, milky colour or burnt smell.
  • Split tractors only on proper stands, never on jacks or loaders.
  • Only the mechanic gives signals when moving heavy sections.
  • Keep shims with their parts and cover open housings.
